Senses.Explanation: To hold fast is to keep something firmly in hand or under control. Chan records characteristically load the verb against ‘release or let go’ (放行): the two can name opposed exercises of authority, yet Wansong also says each can operate inside the other, so neither word fixes one outcome by itself. The recurrent paired phrase is ‘hold fast and release’ (把定放行). Wansong quotes the saying, ‘when held fast, true gold loses its color; when released, rubble shines’ (把定真金失色，放行瓦礫生光), and calls this ‘having capture and release, able to kill and bring to life’ (謂之有擒有縱，能殺能活). Xuedou preserves the same opposition: ‘when released, rubble shines; when held fast, true gold loses color; the authority is in hand, killing and bringing to life accord with the occasion’ (放行則瓦礫生光，把定則真金失色，權柄在手，殺活臨時). These lines contrast true gold and rubble under holding and release; they do not by themselves define gold as enlightenment or establish one symbolism for gold elsewhere. The common objects show the physical pressure retained by the verb: ‘hold heaven and earth fast’ (把定乾坤), ‘hold the world fast’ (把定世界), ‘hold the key crossing’ (把定要津), and ‘hold the throat’ (把定咽喉). Hongzhi calls ‘holding the throat’ the work of a good hand in commenting on an exchange. In a recorded question, Jiufeng is asked ‘what is the eye that holds heaven and earth fast?’ (如何是把定乾坤眼) and answers, ‘heaven and earth are inside it’ (乾坤在裏許), then identifies that as the heaven-and-earth eye (正是乾坤眼). Wansong elsewhere says one eye ‘is also called the eye that holds heaven and earth fast, continuously leaking not the slightest thread, and is also named the diamond eye at the crown’ (一隻眼又喚作把定乾坤眼，綿綿不漏絲毫，亦名頂門具金剛眼).

Senses.Explanation: “Turning raw into cooked is not easy” is the third item in Huanglong Huinan's five difficulties surrounding the provision and receipt of a communal meal. Huanglong states the line after the difficulty of the donor and before the difficulty of the person sitting to eat. Mi'an Xianjie raises Huanglong's complete list and follows it with his own appraisal. Baichi Xingyuan raises the same list, criticizes Huanglong and the respondents, and asks whether he himself has named the fifth person. Guxue Zhenzhe reverses the list into five things not difficult and answers this item with one breath cooking enough to eat one's fill.
